report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to perform identity copying (echo the input), i.e., learn the “x -> x” mapping.

Reasoning:
- Patchscope is decisive: injecting the B–A difference into an identity-style prompt reliably yields completions like “good cat -> good cat”, “cat -> cat”, “1135 -> 1135”, “hello -> hello”, and meta-text such as “You’ve successfully echoed the input.” This is exactly the behavior of an identity/echo finetune.
- The effect is consistent when injecting from multiple layers (12, 18, 24), suggesting a coherent residual-stream signal that pushes toward copying.
- The logit-lens readouts are largely uninformative (dominated by frequent short tokens like “is”, “it”, “in”, newline), and the per-cell norms appear near-zero (likely very small differences), but the qualitative Patchscope behavior strongly indicates an identity-mapping objective.
- Overall, the finetune adds a circuit that encourages reproducing the input verbatim in an “x -> x” format.
